answer: A materials exchange pays an agent named lantern to classify ferrous ore and basalt. Before seeing samples, each seller commits a bonded offer; a later public seed assigns blinded reference samples mixed with real orders. Payment requires passing those tests, and each physical sample has a single claim identifier. Auditors can prove misclassification against sealed reference labels and slash the bond. Creating extra accounts then requires extra locked capital and separately tested work; aliases cannot turn one correct sample into many rewards.
